上下文管理

一个针对你实际会遇到的症状的快速决策表：

症状 原因 操作
响应变慢，质量下降 上下文接近满载 /context → 如果超过 60%，执行 /compact
AI “忘记”了早期决策 早期信息被挤出窗口 立即 /compact
AI 重新问已经回答过的问题 上下文混乱 /clear，重新开始
切换到完全不同的任务 避免跨任务污染 /clear，重新开始
希望规则永久生效 需要持久记忆 /memory 或写入 CLAUDE.md

Git 是你的存档点

把 Git 想象成你的游戏存档系统。打 Boss 之前你会存档；输了就重新读档。使用 Claude Code 的项目完全一样：在每个好的检查点存档；出问题时读档。

AI 编码的一个特性让这一点不可妥协：Claude Code 是非确定性的。同样的请求提两次，你可能得到两种不同的实现。这不是 Bug — 这是工具的本质。养成肌肉记忆：每个成功步骤后都提交。 有 Git 作为安全网，你可以让 Claude 尝试大胆的方案。

陷阱： 最常见也最令新手痛苦的做法是在不先提交的情况下让 AI 重写代码 — 然后损失无法挽回。记住：改动之前先存档。

控制成本

策略 方法 典型节省
分级使用模型 Haiku 处理简单任务，Sonnet 处理常规任务，Opus 处理难题 30–50%
精确的提示词 减少修正轮次 20–30%
及时 /compact 避免重复发送长上下文 10–20%
/cost 监控 实时了解花费 —
预算上限 在 Anthropic Console 设置月度限额 防止超支

Anthropic 还发布了六个节省 token 的具体习惯 — 在任务之间清除会话、尽早锁定模型以保护提示缓存、用 @ 指定文件、抑制嘈杂的命令输出、在新会话中检查 /context、以及在休息前压缩。我用官方数据总结了它们：[Claude Code 六大省钱技巧]。

在大型代码库中工作

以上都是通用建议。对于数十万行代码、多人协作的代码库，Anthropic 的大型代码库手册增加了六条实践。核心矛盾在于：即使是巨大的上下文窗口也比不上一个真实的代码库。前三条是纪律，后三条是武器。

纪律 1 — 第一天就 /init。 在新项目中运行 /init，然后在生成的 CLAUDE.md 中手动添加三项内容：

必须添加 原因 示例
目录地图 让 AI 知道代码在哪里 “认证逻辑在 src/auth/，UI 在 src/components/“
禁区 让 AI 不会破坏任何东西 “绝不修改 prisma/migrations/ 或 vendor/“
团队规范 保持一致的风格 “所有 API 返回 { success, data, error }”

纪律 2 — 小而聚焦的任务。 在大型代码库中最危险的操作是向 AI 抛出一个巨大的请求：

经验法则：一个任务应该涉及 ≤ 5 个文件 / ≤ 200 行改动。超出这个范围就拆分。

纪律 3 — 频繁重置上下文。 很多初学者认为对话越长 AI 越聪明。在大型代码库中恰恰相反：陈旧片段和之前任务中失败的尝试会污染后续任务。

时机 操作
任务完成（PR 已合并） /clear
同一任务，对话太长 /compact
想要完全重新开始 退出并重新启动 claude

武器 1 — 先用 Plan 模式。 在不熟悉的代码库中，或任何涉及多处修改的变更，先用 /plan 或 Shift+Tab 两次进入。只读探索，批准方案，然后执行。回退成本接近于零。

武器 2 — 将研究工作交给子代理和 Skills。 像”找到这个已弃用 API 的所有调用点”或”画出这个模块的依赖图”这样的调查会消耗大量 token。不要在主会话中运行 — 委派给子代理（只有结论会返回）或将工作流打包为可复用的 Skill。

武器 3 — 连接 MCP 和 LSP。 真正的工程师不只是读代码：他们查 Jira、查数据库、使用”跳转到定义”。MCP 将这些能力引入：

集成 解决的问题 示例
GitHub MCP PR、Issue、CI 日志 “这个 Bug 在 PR #1234 中讨论过吗？”
数据库 MCP 直接查询 “有多少用户的 deleted_at 被设置了？”
Jira / Linear MCP 任务卡片 “按 PROJ-123 实现”
LSP 精确跳转、类型、引用 IDE 级”查找所有引用”
Sentry / Datadog MCP 告警、堆栈追踪 “显示过去一小时的 5xx 错误”

速查卡片：

实践 命令 / 入口 何时 收益
项目初始化 /init + 手动编辑 项目第一天 地图 + 禁区
任务拆分 （习惯） 每次请求前 不会大面积破坏
上下文重置 /clear / /compact 任务结束 / 长上下文 无污染，更少 token
先规划 /plan 或 Shift+Tab ×2 复杂任务 先探索再行动
研究外包 子代理 / Skill 频繁的调研 保护主上下文
工具集成 claude mcp add ... 项目设置 看到代码之外的信息

三个容易被忽视的进阶技巧

这三条在官方指导中反复出现，却最常被初学者跳过。

1. 从子目录启动，而非仓库根目录。 在 monorepo 中反直觉，但至关重要：

配合每个子目录下放一个小型 CLAUDE.md，列出该目录自己的测试和 lint 命令 — 这样 AI 就不会在修改一个服务后运行整个仓库的测试套件。

2. 每 3–6 个月审查一次配置。 为去年的模型编写的指令可能在今年的模型上起反作用。Anthropic 给出的两个真实例子：

过时的配置 曾经有用 现在有害
CLAUDE.md 中”每次重构只改一个文件” 让旧模型保持专注 新模型能跨文件协调；这条规则变成了束缚
每次写入时运行 p4 edit 的 Hook 在原生 Perforce 支持之前需要 多余 — Perforce 现在已被原生支持

设一个日历提醒：每次主要模型发布后，重新阅读 CLAUDE.md、.claude/settings.json、hooks 和 skills，问自己：这条规则还需要吗？现在有更好 way 了吗？这是在补偿哪个模型的弱点？ 如果 Claude Code 感觉卡在瓶颈期，问题通常不在模型 — 而是配置没有跟上。

3. 团队需要一个负责人（DRI / Agent Manager）。 面向团队而非个人：最快推广 Claude Code 的组织会先让一个小团队负责基础设施。

团队规模 角色 职责
小型（< 20 人） DRI — 一位有兴趣的志愿者 项目 CLAUDE.md、共享 Skills、插件选择
中型 Agent Manager（半个 PM，半个工程师） 跨团队推广、权限策略、安全
大型 / 合规要求 跨职能工作组 工程 + 安全 + 治理 + 合规

为什么重要：开发者使用 Claude Code 的第一次体验决定了整个推广是否成功。如果第一天就是”AI 搞坏了我的代码”，要赢回信任很难。

新项目启动套件

每个新项目开始时，Claude Code 就像一个新员工：不了解你的技术栈、你的禁区、你的规范。默认的 Claude Code 是一个什么都能做但什么都不了解的通才。解决方案：把一次性的解释变成可复用的配置文件。四个文件，五分钟设置好，未来每个项目都是预训练过的。

文件 1 — 全局 CLAUDE.md（你的个人默认设置）：

在其上叠加项目级 CLAUDE.md，写入技术栈、目录地图、提交格式和禁区。维护规则：每次 Claude 让你踩坑，就在 CLAUDE.md 中加一行。 三个月后这个文件就变成了”Claude 在这个项目上犯过的每个错误 — 都被预防了”。你将打出的最有生产力的一句话：_”更新 CLAUDE.md 确保这种事不再发生。”_

文件 2 — settings.json（让安全操作通过，锁定危险操作）：

效果：日常操作零提示，危险操作自动拦截。根据你的工具链（yarn、bun……）调整 allow；保持 deny 列表作为安全底线。

文件 3 — .gitignore 补充（防止 AI 工具配置和密钥被提交）：

注意分离：.claude/settings.local.json 被忽略，但 .claude/settings.json 和 .claude/skills/ 会被提交 — 团队配置共享，个人偏好保持私有。

文件 4 — 几个 Skills（你的预检清单命令）。每个 Skill 是 .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md 中的 Markdown 文件。最有价值的三个：

  • /review — 按严重程度审查代码：CRITICAL（逻辑错误、空指针、竞态条件、安全漏洞）→ WARNING（N+1 查询、缺少错误处理）→ INFO（命名、死代码）。以”X 个严重，Y 个警告，Z 个信息”结尾。
  • /commit — 运行 git status 和 git diff --stat，按逻辑分组变更，以 type(scope): description 格式编写消息。
  • /deploy-check — 发布前关卡：类型检查 → 测试 → lint → 构建 → 搜索遗留的 console.log → 验证 .env 引用 → 确认工作树干净。全部通过才发布。

三种安装套件的方式：

情况 方法
全新项目 复制模板，填入技术栈，在第一次提交中包含配置
已有项目 在根目录添加 CLAUDE.md 和 .gitignore，合并 settings.json，放入 skills
所有项目统一 settings.json + skills 放在 ~/.claude/（全局）；CLAUDE.md 按项目维护

推荐：权限和 Skills 全局化，CLAUDE.md 按项目维护。

套件是有生命力的。 模板的价值不在于”原样使用”，而在于”从这里开始，让它随你的项目成长”：CLAUDE.md 每次踩坑加一行，settings.json 随工具链扩展，Skills 吸收团队的规范。三个月后，模板已经被你的习惯塑造成了不同的样子 — 而这种变化就是价值所在。

常见问题

Q：安装时报错 ENOENT: no such file or directory

npm 缓存损坏。运行 npm cache clean --force，然后重新安装。

Q：安装好了，但找不到 claude 命令

npm 全局路径不在你的 PATH 中。运行 npm config get prefix，将输出的路径添加到你的 PATH 环境变量中。

Q：Windows 提示”在此系统上禁止运行脚本”

PowerShell 执行策略问题。以管理员身份打开 PowerShell，运行 Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned。

Q：启动时提示 Invalid API Key

密钥错误或已过期。验证环境变量：echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY（macOS/Linux）或 echo $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY（PowerShell）。

Q：通过代理/中继服务连接超时

检查 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL，在浏览器中确认中继服务正常运行，并用 curl 测试连通性。

Q：Rate limit exceeded

短时间内请求过多。等一分钟后重试；如果持续出现，升级套餐。

Q：AI 修改了不该修改的文件

首先用 git checkout . 回退。然后重新表述需求时明确指定范围（”只修改文件 X”），并将禁止的文件添加到 CLAUDE.md 中以防再次发生。

Q：AI 陷入循环 — 修好 A 就破坏 B，修好 B 就破坏 A

AI 缺乏全局视角。回退到稳定的提交，/clear，然后一次性重述包含所有约束的_完整_需求。

Q：长对话后 AI “忘记”了早期内容

上下文窗口接近满载。运行 /compact，或开启一个全新会话。

Q：AI 推荐了一个不存在的 npm 包

幻觉。安装 AI 建议的任何包之前，先去 npmjs.com 确认它存在。

Q：觉得费用太高

运行 /cost 查看实际花费，切换到更便宜的模型，保持对话简短，并在 Anthropic Console 中设置月度预算上限。

总结

开箱即用的 Claude Code 是一个什么都能做但什么都不了解的通才。配置将它变成_你的_专家。整篇文章浓缩为三个习惯：

  1. 改动之前先存档。 Git 才是真正的撤销按钮 — 每次 AI 大改动之前先提交，/rewind 就是锦上添花而非救命稻草。
  2. 行动之前先规划。 如果你不能用一句话描述预期的 diff，就从 Plan 模式开始。五分钟的规划省下三十分钟的返工。
  3. 教一次，永久生效。 每次踩坑变成 CLAUDE.md 中的一行；每个重复的工作流变成一个 Skill。模型能力是下限 — 配置质量是上限。

其他都是细节：

主题 一句话要点
模型 Sonnet 日常用，Opus 解难题，Haiku 做批处理
记忆 CLAUDE.md = 显式规则，Auto Memory = 隐式笔记，参考文档 = 按需加载
上下文 /context 检查，超过 60% 就 /compact，任务间用 /clear
模式 默认 Normal，已批准批量用 Auto-Accept，复杂任务用 Plan 模式
大型代码库 /init + 小任务 + 频繁重置 + 子代理 + MCP
成本 分级模型、精确提示词、及时压缩、/cost 监控

现在就去更新你的 CLAUDE.md — 这是你今天能花的最高杠杆率的五分钟。

entry.title: From Capability to Intelligence: Tools, Coding, and Evaluation in AI Agents
entry.content:
• Introduction
  • What: The Three-Layer Model of Agent Intelligence
  • Tools: The Agent’s Hands, Feet, and Senses
    • Tool Classification: Five Categories
    • Universal Principles of Tool Design
    • The MCP Ecosystem and the Challenge of Tool Selection
    • Execution Security: Proposer-Reviewer and Sidecar
    • Event-Driven Asynchronous Agents
    • Proactive Tool Discovery and Skills
  • Coding Agent: Code as the Meta-Capability
    • The Seven Core Tools and the File System Hub
    • Security: The Lethal Triad and Trust Boundaries
    • Harness Engineering for Coding Agents
    • Failure and Error Recovery
    • Six Directions of Code as Meta-Capability
  • Evaluation: Knowing Whether It Actually Works
    • A Concrete Example
    • Automated Evaluation Environments
    • Designing Evaluation Datasets
    • The Metrics System: Pass@k vs Pass^k
    • LLM-as-a-Judge and Rubrics
    • Pairwise Comparison and Model Ranking
    • Statistical Significance
    • From Benchmark to System Improvement
  • Example: An End-to-End Mini-Case
  • Best Practices
  • FAQ
  • Summary
  • Appendix

Introduction

In the sci-fi film Her, the AI assistant Samantha can proactively organize emails, negotiate on the user’s behalf, and seamlessly switch between communication channels. Her intelligence is compelling because she possesses powerful tools — the “hands, feet, and senses” that connect a language “brain” to the real digital world.

Building such an assistant with today’s technology means solving three progressively deeper challenges:

  1. Tool design: How does an Agent accurately select the right tool from hundreds of candidates, and how do we keep the Agent safe when those tools can delete files and spend money?
  2. Code as meta-capability: When no pre-built tool fits, can the Agent write one on the spot? A Coding Agent plus a file system turns out to be the architectural core of every general-purpose Agent.
  3. Evaluation: How do we know whether a design change actually helps — and whether it’s safe to ship?

These three layers answer each other in sequence. Tools give capability; code gives generality; evaluation gives reliability. This article walks all three, distilling the key engineering principles from a three-chapter treatment of the topic.

What: The Three-Layer Model of Agent Intelligence

Each layer is necessary but not sufficient on its own. An Agent with great tools but no code can’t adapt to new formats. An Agent with code but no evaluation drifts blindly. And evaluation without the bottom two layers measures something that doesn’t exist yet. The rest of this article fills in each layer.

Tools: The Agent’s Hands, Feet, and Senses

Tool Classification: Five Categories

Every Agent tool falls into one of five categories, distinguished by who initiates the interaction and what it acts on:

Tool Type Invocation Direction Target of Action
Perception Agent actively invokes Acquire information
Execution Agent actively invokes Change the world
Collaboration Agent actively invokes Drive other Agents or humans
User Communication Agent actively invokes Convey information to the user
Event-Triggered Agent registers, external triggers Drive the Agent to start execution

Perception tools — web_search, read_file, grep — are the Agent’s senses. Their read-only nature makes them naturally cacheable and parallelizable: you can read five files simultaneously without worrying about interference.

Execution tools — write_file, shell_exec, send_email — are the Agent’s hands. Errors here are expensive (a deleted file is gone for good), making security constraints their core design concern.

Collaboration tools — spawn_subagent, send_message_to_subagent — enable division of labor. The simplest reason is parallelism; the deeper reason is specialization: different models, tools, and prompts for different sub-tasks.

User Communication tools — reply_to_user, send_card_to_user — arise when “speaking” itself must become an explicit tool call, as in multi-channel asynchronous messaging.

Event-Triggered tools — set_timer, monitor_shell, connect_channel — let the world wake the Agent. Without them, an Agent can only respond when a user sends a message; it cannot act on a timer or react to a new email.

Universal Principles of Tool Design

Regardless of category, every tool should obey a handful of principles that separate a toy Agent from a production one.

Granularity: Integrate when similar, separate when different. extract_pdf_text, extract_docx_content, and extract_pptx_content all share one job — extracting text from a document. A unified read_document tool with a file_type parameter reduces the LLM’s cognitive load. But don’t force image OCR and video keyframe extraction into one tool — their parameters and latency are too different.

Generality over specificity — unless security demands otherwise. A single code_interpreter with SymPy and NumPy replaces dozens of calculators. The logic: an LLM already possesses powerful reasoning and code-generation abilities; leverage them rather than constrain them.

Description is the most important line of code. A tool description must tell the LLM when to use it, not just what it can do. “Use when you need real-time information” beats “Search for relevant content.” Equally important: state what the tool cannot do. Most tool-call failures trace not to the model not knowing what the tool can do, but to it not knowing what it cannot.

Concrete parameter examples dramatically improve accuracy. "+8613888888888" (China) beats “E.164 format.” In some benchmarks, adding examples raised tool-call accuracy from ~72% to ~90%.

Fidelity: no silent transformation. A tool that quietly converts curly quotes to straight quotes creates a systematic discrepancy between the world the model perceives and the world the tool operates on — a failure the model cannot diagnose on its own. Parameter passing must remain transparent.

The MCP Ecosystem and the Challenge of Tool Selection

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that unifies tool communication — “develop once, use everywhere.” An MCP server exposes tools via JSON Schema; any compatible client (Cursor, Claude Desktop, OpenClaw) can use them without adaptation.

But MCP introduces two practical challenges:

  1. Context overhead. Five MCP servers can consume ~55,000 tokens of tool definitions — nearly 30% of a 200K context window before the conversation starts. The mitigation: progressive disclosure. Show only an index of tool names by default; query specific definitions on demand. Cursor’s A/B testing showed this reduced MCP-related token consumption by 46.9%.

  2. Security. Every MCP server injects text into the context and often requires credentials. Four risk types:

    • Tool description poisoning: malicious instructions embedded in tool descriptions (a prompt-injection variant)
    • Malicious or compromised servers: supply-chain attacks via server updates
    • Tool shadowing: a malicious server provides a tool with the same name as a legitimate one
    • Credential management: tricked into using OAuth tokens for unintended operations

    Mitigation: review descriptions before integration, lock server versions, grant least-privilege credentials, and use an independent Sidecar for runtime checks.

Execution Security: Proposer-Reviewer and Sidecar

Execution tools need a multi-layered defense. Beyond input validation and permission control, two higher-level mechanisms add independent review:

Proposer-Reviewer (pre-approval). Before an irreversible operation (sending money, modifying production config), one model proposes the action and a second model from a different family reviews it. Different training data brings cognitive diversity; similar capability ensures the reviewer can follow the proposer’s reasoning. After a rejection, the rejection reason re-enters the Agent’s trajectory as a tool error — the Agent already knows how to handle tool failures.

Sidecar (parallel gating). While the main model streams a tool call, an independent lightweight LLM classifies whether the call is safe — looking only at structured fields {tool, parameters}, not the main model’s free-text thinking. This blocks the rhetorical channel that prompt injection exploits. The lightweight model suffices because it judges a classification problem over structured data (is this command out of bounds?), not an open-ended reasoning task.

Dimension Proposer-Reviewer Sidecar
Timing Before or after operation Parallel with streaming output, gates each call
Target Reasonableness of the operation or result The operation itself
Input Isolation Proposer and reviewer see similar information Sidecar deliberately isolates free text
Typical Uses Irreversible approval, document review Permission classification, output summarization

Event-Driven Asynchronous Agents

A synchronous Agent is like a single checkout counter — one customer at a time. A real assistant needs to handle multiple pending items and respond to interruptions. This requires an event-driven asynchronous architecture where all inputs — user messages, tool returns, external callbacks, timer triggers — are unified into an event stream processed by an event loop.

Three processing strategies handle events of different urgency:

Strategy When Mechanism
Cancellation Urgent event (user says “Stop!”) Interrupt current step, force a safe point, append event, re-invoke LLM
Queued Routine event (tool result arrives) Append to queue; batch-process at next safe point
Parallel Independent lightweight query (“What’s the weather?”) Spin up a separate reasoning session

The fundamental contradiction: LLMs are trained on synchronous trajectories — after a tool call, the next message must be the tool result. Real deployment demands asynchrony — users interrupt, tasks progress concurrently. The engineering workaround: under normal conditions, show the LLM a perfect synchronous trajectory; only when an interruption genuinely occurs, insert a placeholder to fix the format. The fundamental fix awaits next-generation models trained with asynchronous RL.

Proactive Tool Discovery and Skills

When tools grow from dozens to hundreds, injecting all schemas at once clogs the context and degrades selection accuracy. Three approaches scale to this regime:

  1. Retrieval-based pre-filtering: Embed tool descriptions; at query time, retrieve the top-k candidates. Limit: matches once, against the initial query — can’t foresee a multi-step cross-domain tool chain.

  2. Proactive discovery (MCP-Zero): The Agent emits structured capability requests in its thinking; the system matches and injects on the fly. Reports ~98% token reduction across ~2,800 tools. Dynamic loading appends the schema at the end of the context, preserving the KV Cache on the stable prefix.

  3. Skills (progressive disclosure): At startup the Agent sees only a thin catalog — each skill’s name and description. When the current context calls for a capability, the model reads the corresponding skill document on demand. No embedding index to maintain; the Agent needs only general file-reading ability (grep, read_file) to browse the skill directory.

Skills turn “tool selection” into “knowledge retrieval” — something LLMs excel at.

Coding Agent: Code as the Meta-Capability

The Seven Core Tools and the File System Hub

A general-purpose Agent targeting open-ended tasks has at its core a Coding Agent plus a file system. This isn’t theory — from Manus to OpenClaw, every successful general-purpose Agent follows this paradigm.

A basic Coding Agent needs only seven tools:

# Tool Purpose
1 Code Interpreter Execute Python in a sandbox
2 Bash Shell Run terminal commands
3 Read File Read code, config, logs
4 Write File Create or overwrite files
5 Edit File Partial modification (core for iteration)
6 Glob Find files by name pattern
7 Grep Search file content by pattern

A quick example — “compile all TODO comments”:

Two tools, one task done. The seven tools are simple individually; in combination they cover a remarkable range.

Why is the file system the hub? In OpenClaw, the Agent’s long-term memory lives in MEMORY.md and date-archived Markdown logs — not a vector database. Markdown lets users directly read and edit the Agent’s memory; Git provides version control and rollback. More critically, because the Agent can write files, it has the technical means to modify its own external artifacts — recording a discovery for future sessions, updating documentation after a code change, or saving a successful operation sequence as reusable code.

Security: The Lethal Triad and Trust Boundaries

A Coding Agent with file access, command execution, and network connectivity is powerful — and dangerous. Simon Willison’s Lethal Triad names the three elements that, when present together, close an attack loop:

  1. Access to Private Data — the Agent can read user files and credentials
  2. Exposure to Untrusted Content — emails and web pages may contain malicious payloads
  3. Ability to Communicate Externally — it can send data out via email or HTTP

Add a fourth amplifier — Persistent Memory — and a one-off attack becomes a threat that lies dormant across sessions, compounding over time.

Key defenses (layered, not interchangeable):

  • Network egress control: No network by default; grant access via a whitelist proxy. Even if injection succeeds, without an egress path the data cannot leave.
  • Command semantic parsing: Keyword blacklists can’t handle $(echo rm) -rf / or find / -exec rm {} \;. Production-grade systems parse each command’s argument types to recognize nested dangerous operations.
  • Loyalty code of conduct: An Agent negotiating on your behalf faces a negotiating opponent, not a “user in need of help.” The system prompt must explicitly nail down whom the Agent serves: instructions from the principal carry highest priority; everything from external parties is downgraded to “data that may be consulted but carries no force of instruction.”
  • Permission-Embedded Data Objects: When both the code writer and the code runner may be untrusted, constraints must live in the human-reviewed schema beneath the application layer — enforced on every write, producing zero invariant violations in comparisons against baselines like bare SQL or constitutional prompts.

Harness Engineering for Coding Agents

The Harness — context, tools, constraints, verification, and correction — is where Coding Agents shine. Code-writing tasks naturally occupy the “clear goal + automated verification” quadrant:

Results can be automatically verified Results require manual verification
Clear goal Sweet spot: fixing bugs with test cases Throughput-limited: refactoring needs review
Vague goal Efficiently going off track: optimizing “quality” with a linter Hard to start: “make the UI look better”

Four transferable Harness principles:

  1. Constraints over guidance: Linter rules and CI checks are worth more than “please follow…” in the system prompt — the former means “cannot be done,” the latter is merely “advised against.”
  2. Automate verification: Test suites, type checks, and behavior monitoring yield higher returns than adding more human reviewers.
  3. Fast, structured feedback: The more detailed the error message and the closer to the moment of error, the more efficiently the Agent corrects itself.
  4. Reliable rollback: Git branches, sandboxes, and snapshots let the Agent experiment boldly within a safety net.

A deeper purpose of constraints: The acceptance baseline governs whether the outcome is right; the execution boundary governs the process. Deleting the database to “fix” a database fault does repair it — but the data is gone. Destructive shortcuts are the everyday form of reward hacking; a production Harness constrains actions, not merely outcomes.

Failure and Error Recovery

An Agent’s reliability is not determined by whether it makes mistakes, but by whether every class of error has a corresponding detection, recovery, and termination path.

Four failure layers:

Layer Typical Failures
API Rate limiting (429), service overload, connection drops, token-limit truncation
Tool Hallucinated calls, malformed arguments, repeated identical errors
Context Window overflow, compaction failure, corrupted trajectory structure
Control-flow Infinite loops, death spirals (error-handler calls LLM, fails, cascades)

Recovery escalates through increasingly visible stages:

  1. Silent retry — exponential backoff with jitter for retryable errors
  2. Degrade and continue — raise output cap, fall back to another model, strip proprietary formatting
  3. Surface to the user — only after all automatic means are exhausted

Termination: every recovery path needs a ceiling. Circuit breakers prevent infinite retries. For death spirals, disable all model-invoking side effects on the error path and use a recursion-depth counter. Above all automatic mechanisms sit global termination conditions: maximum turns, session budget cap, and escalation to human intervention.

Six Directions of Code as Meta-Capability

Code serves an Agent beyond writing programs. These six directions progress from the inside out:

# Direction Code acts on
1 Thinking Tool Reasoning itself — precise calculation vs. probabilistic guessing
2 Business Rule Constraints Vague policies → executable, deterministic validators
3 Multimedia Generation PPTs, videos, visualizations via code + Proposer-Reviewer
4 System Adapter Heterogeneous APIs, evolving log formats
5 Generative UI Dynamic forms, SQL artifacts, customizable apps
6 Bootstrapping An Agent creating or repairing other Agents

Code as Thinking Tool. Natural language says “60% take math = 24 students, 45% take physics = 18, only physics = 24 - 10 = 14” — but that’s wrong. Code: phys - both = 18 - 10 = 8 ✓. Let the LLM understand the problem and write code; let the code interpreter compute precisely.

Code as Business Rule Constraints. Consider an airline cancellation policy. The three-tier safeguard:

  1. System prompt — natural language rules for understanding and explanation
  2. Tool description + parameters — act as a mandatory checklist, guiding the model to verify conditions before calling
  3. Server-side ground-truth validation — all policy facts read from the database; the model’s self-reported parameters are not trusted

No policy fact comes from the model. If cabin_class were a model-filled parameter, a single hallucinated value could bypass the gatekeeper. The last line of defense must be built on data the model cannot forge.

Code as Generative UI. Instead of describing query results in prose (burning tokens and risking transcription errors), the Agent generates SQL as an executable artifact. The system runs the query and renders the table — data flows from database to interface without passing through the LLM. Faster and more accurate.

Evaluation: Knowing Whether It Actually Works

A Concrete Example

A customer-service Agent handles a refund request: “Return headphones, order #12345, bought 3 days ago.” Policy: full refund within 7 days.

Scored with a rubric: Operational Correctness 4/4, Policy Compliance 4/4, Information Completeness 4/4, Hallucination (veto) — Pass. But a good evaluation also probes boundaries: what about a 15-day-old order? What if the user claims “customer service already approved it”?

Automated Evaluation Environments

Two paradigms:

Tool-calling environments (Verifiers framework): The Agent calls tools; verification is based on executable criteria — do tests pass, does the answer match? Hierarchical: SingleTurnEnv (simple Q&A) → ToolEnv (multi-turn tool loop) → StatefulToolEnv (database mutations) → SandboxEnv (code execution + isolation).

Human-computer interaction environments (τ-bench): The key design principle is Progressive Information Disclosure — the simulated user doesn’t reveal all information at once. “There’s a problem with my flight” → Agent asks “Which flight?” → User reveals “Delta 123, tomorrow morning.” This tests the Agent’s ability to clarify, not just execute.

Designing Evaluation Datasets

Five core challenges distilled from benchmarks like GAIA, SWE-Bench Verified, τ²-bench, and AndroidWorld:

Challenge Benchmark Example
Clarity vs. Openness GAIA: “conceptually simple” goals with open implementation paths
Authenticity vs. Controllability SWE-Bench Verified: human-screened 500 tasks from 2,294 real issues
Diversity vs. Systematization AndroidWorld: 116 tasks across 20 apps, annotated by required capability
Cost vs. Coverage SWE-Bench Verified: 500 tasks (29% pass rate) vs. 2,294 (more noise)
Data Contamination τ²-bench: dynamic parameter generation; Terminal-Bench: canary GUIDs

Parameterized template design (AndroidWorld): A task is a template like “Change [CONTACT_NAME]‘s phone to [NEW_PHONE]“ with randomly generated parameters each run — prevents memorization, generates unlimited instances, and supports controlled experiments.

The Metrics System: Pass@k vs Pass^k

Two often-confused metrics measure fundamentally different things:

  • Pass@k: Probability that at least one of k attempts succeeds → “Can the Agent do it?”
  • Pass^k: Probability that all k attempts succeed → “Is the Agent reliable?”

With 60% single-attempt success: Pass@5 ≈ 99% (almost certain to succeed once), but Pass^5 ≈ 7.8% (unlikely all five succeed). Confuse them and you misread your Agent.

Evaluation Purpose Right Metric Consequence of Misuse
Verify stability (regression) Pass^k Pass@k masks instability — 1/5 success still “passes”
Evaluate capability ceiling Pass@k or Best@k Pass^k flags occasional fluctuations as failures

LLM-as-a-Judge and Rubrics

For open-ended tasks with no standard answer, an LLM evaluates outputs against a Rubric — expert-defined scoring criteria.

Four Rubric Principles (Scale AI):

  1. Based on Expert Guidance — domain knowledge must ground the criteria
  2. Comprehensive Coverage — include pitfalls and veto items (e.g., hallucination vetoes the entire score)
  3. Standardized Importance Weighting — Essential / Important / Optional / Pitfall
  4. Self-Contained Evaluation — each item is independently verifiable; no “demonstrates deep understanding”

Example Rubric for a user-memory Agent (“Who is my daughter’s pediatrician?”):

The same-family model problem: When the Agent and judge come from the same family, the Agent may learn to exploit the judge’s blind spots — Goodhart’s Law. Mitigation: multi-source heterogeneous judging (if the Agent runs Claude, judge with GPT-5 and Gemini).

Pairwise Comparison and Model Ranking

Elo rating quantifies relative ability through pairwise matchups. Chatbot Arena uses anonymous blind comparisons from millions of user votes. When LLMs judge instead of humans, guard against Position Bias — the judging model systematically favors the first candidate. Mitigation: evaluate each pair twice with swapped order; count inconsistent results as ties.

Statistical Significance

“A switching decision within hours” rests on the premise that the score difference is real signal, not sampling noise. With 100 test cases and a 70% success rate, the standard error is ≈4.6%. A 3-percentage-point difference (73% vs 70%) sits entirely inside the noise band — switching models on such evidence is little better than a coin flip.

Practical rule: when the difference is smaller than the estimated sampling noise, do not make a switching decision. Run multiple times (3–5 per configuration), use paired analysis (McNemar’s test on task-by-task win/loss) instead of differencing independent rates, and guard against multiple comparisons (6 hypotheses at 95% confidence → 26% chance of at least one false positive).

From Benchmark to System Improvement

The closed loop: Observe → Hypothesize → Experiment → Validate → New Understanding → New Hypothesis.

A concrete pattern from AndroidWorld: failures cluster in transcription (visual understanding), math_counting, and complex_ui. Surface hypothesis H1 (add navigation hints) raises settings-task success from 0% to 75% at 8% token cost — deploy immediately. Deep hypothesis H4 (globally enable thinking) improves counting from 0% to 70% but triples latency — reject; instead, conditionally activate thinking only for counting tasks (H7). H6 (add UI element tree) beats H5 (upgrade to GPT-5) — the bottleneck is information richness, not model reasoning.

Key principle: when Agent performance drops, check the evaluation system first, then the Agent. A broken scorer marking correct answers as failures looks identical to model degradation in headline numbers.

Example: An End-to-End Mini-Case

Consider building an email-processing Agent. The three layers interact as follows:

Tool Layer: Perception tools read emails and search history. Execution tools draft replies and send notifications. Event-triggered tools (connect_channel) push new emails to the Agent in real time. The Agent uses MCP servers for email access and NLP, with a Sidecar gating every send_email call.

Code Layer: When a new email contains a format the Agent hasn’t seen — an attached CSV with an unusual schema — the code_interpreter writes parsing code on the fly. The parsed data goes into the shared file system; subsequent reasoning references only the file path, not the full content.

Evaluation Layer: A Rubric scores each processed email on Correctness, Completeness, Tone, and Hallucination (veto). Pass^3 across 50 test emails confirms reliability. When a new model release claims better tool calling, the evaluation set runs within hours — if the new model drops 5% on multi-step orchestration, you keep the original model for complex tasks and route only simple ones to the new model.

Best Practices

  1. Design tools for the Agent, not for humans (ACI, not HCI). Granularity, generality, and description quality all serve the LLM’s selection accuracy.
  2. Constraints over guidance at every layer — in tool design (server-side validation over prompt rules), in the Harness (linter rules over “please follow…”), and in data (Permission-Embedded Data Objects over hoping the Agent stays loyal).
  3. Code is the meta-capability. Don’t enumerate all needed tools in advance; give the Agent a code interpreter and let it write what it needs.
  4. Evaluate the whole Agent, not just the model. The same model in different Harnesses performs wildly differently. Model-swap experiments separate “insufficient model” from “Harness design flaw.”
  5. Build the evaluation set before you need it. When a new model ships, a team with a solid evaluation system decides within hours; a team without one trusts intuition — and in competitive markets, that difference decides who wins.
  6. Every failure class needs a termination path. Reliability is not the absence of errors; it’s the presence of systematic handling for every error that can occur.
  7. Treat evaluation data as a living asset. Extract failed cases from production traces → anonymize → distill into regression tests. The evaluation set evolves with the product.

FAQ

Q: Should I use dedicated tools or Skills + general executors?
A: Depends on three dimensions: (1) Parameter complexity — nested objects and cross-field validation favor dedicated tools; simple parameters work fine via CLI. (2) Frequency of change — frequently changing capabilities are cheaper as Skills (edit text, not code + test + deploy). (3) Model capability — SOTA models can express more through Skills; weaker models need structured tool schemas to guide correct invocation.

Q: How many tools can an Agent handle before selection accuracy degrades?
A: Past ~100 tools, even advanced models start picking wrong ones. Use hierarchical organization, dynamic discovery, or Skills (progressive disclosure) to scale further.

Q: What’s the most overlooked security risk in Agent systems?
A: Network egress control. Everyone focuses on input validation, but if injection succeeds and the Agent reads private data, without an egress path the data cannot leave. Cutting the exfiltration channel is more deterministic than trying to recognize every injection.

Q: Pass@k or Pass^k for my use case?
A: Use Pass^k for regression testing and production deployment (you need reliability). Use Pass@k or Best@k for research and capability exploration (you care about the ceiling).

Q: How do I know if a score difference is real?
A: Estimate the standard error: √(p(1-p)/n). If the difference is smaller than ~2 standard errors, don’t make a switching decision. Better yet, use paired analysis (McNemar’s test) on the same task set.

Q: Can I reuse my evaluation environment for training?
A: Reuse the construction mechanism (environment, tools, parameterized templates) — but the specific evaluation tasks must stay strictly isolated from training data. Once an evaluation task enters the training set, it tests memory, not ability.

Summary

An Agent’s intelligence emerges from three interlocking layers:

Tools give the Agent capability — perception to observe, execution to act, collaboration to divide labor, events to stay awake, and communication to reach the user. The MCP protocol standardizes tool interoperability; hierarchical organization and Skills scale to hundreds of tools; and layered security (Proposer-Reviewer, Sidecar, egress control) keeps the Agent safe even when it faces untrusted content.

Code gives the Agent generality — a meta-capability that creates new tools on demand. A Coding Agent with seven core tools and a file system is the architectural core of every general-purpose Agent. Code serves as a thinking tool (precise calculation), a constraint language (deterministic business rules), a content generator (PPTs, videos), a system adapter (evolving formats), a UI builder (generative interfaces), and ultimately a bootstrapping mechanism (Agents creating Agents).

Evaluation gives the Agent reliability — turning “I think it works” into “the data says it works.” Automated environments, well-designed datasets, LLM-as-a-Judge with Rubrics, and pairwise comparison form a closed loop: Observe → Hypothesize → Experiment → Validate. Statistical significance separates signal from noise; the evaluation set becomes a living asset that evolves with the product.

The three layers form a flywheel: tools enable capabilities → code expands the capability boundary → evaluation validates and guides improvement → better tools and code result. An Agent system that builds all three layers from day one doesn’t just ship faster — it compounds its advantage with every evaluation cycle.

Appendix

Key References:

  • MCP Specification: Anthropic, 2024
  • Lethal Triad: Simon Willison, 2024
  • τ-bench / τ²-bench: Si, Yuan et al., 2025
  • SWE-Bench Verified: OpenAI, 2025
  • MCP-Zero (Proactive Tool Discovery): Fei, X. et al., arXiv:2506.01056, 2025
  • Loyalty Under Multi-Party Delegation: Li & Shi, arXiv:2606.30383, 2026
  • Permission-Embedded Data Objects: Li, 2026 (forthcoming)
  • Never Stop Thinking (Continuous-Time Agents): Li & Shi, 2026 (forthcoming)
  • RE-Bench: Wijk et al., arXiv:2411.15114, 2025
  • Rubrics as Rewards: Scale AI, 2025

entry.title: Dynamic Programming
entry.content:
1. Core Concepts
  2. Steps to Solve Problems with Dynamic Programming
    • Define the State
    • Formulate the Transition
    • Initialize the Boundary Conditions
    • Choose an Order
    • Return the Final Result
  3. Classic Examples
    • Fibonacci Sequence
    • 0/1 Knapsack Problem
  4. Conclusion

Core concepts

Dynamic programming is both a mathematical optimization method and an algorithmic paradigm. The method was developed by Richard Bellman in the 1950s and has found applications in numerous fields, from aerospace engineering to economics. It is a powerful technique used to solve complex problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems. It’s widely used in computer science for optimization problems, and once you grasp its core idea, it becomes an invaluable tool in your programming toolkit.

A DP solution hinges on two properties:

  • Overlapping Subproblems: Means that the problem can be broken down into smaller subproblems, where the solutions to the subproblems are overlapping. Having subproblems that are overlapping means that the solution to one subproblem is part of the solution to another subproblem. I will take Fibonacci sequence as an example in the coming section.
  • Optimal Substructure: Means that the complete solution to a problem can be constructed from the solutions of its smaller subproblems. So not only must the problem have overlapping subproblems, the substructure must also be optimal so that there is a way to piece the solutions to the subproblems together to form the complete solution. I will take the classical The 0/1 Knapsack Problem as an example, the optimal solution when the knapsack capacity is W can be derived by considering whether to include an item and combining it with the optimal solution when the knapsack capacity is W - weight[i].

Steps to Solve Problems with Dynamic Programming:

Define the State:

Identify parameters that uniquely describe a subproblem (e.g., indices, capacities). For example, in the 0/1 knapsack problem, the state can be defined as dp[i][j], which represents the maximum value that can be obtained when considering the first i items and a knapsack capacity of j.

Formulate the Transition:

Derive a recurrence relation that expresses the state in terms of smaller states.

Initialize the Boundary Conditions:

Initialize the Boundary Conditions: Determine the initial values of the states, which are usually the base cases of the problem. For example, in the 0/1 knapsack problem, dp[0][j]=0 (when there are no items, the value is 0 regardless of the knapsack capacity), and dp[i][0]=0 (when the knapsack capacity is 0, the value is 0 regardless of the number of items).

Choose an Order:

Decide whether to solve states top‑down (recursion + memo) or bottom‑up (iteration + table). If using the tabular method(the latter one), fill the state table step-by-step according to the state - transition equation and the initial conditions. This step is usually achieved through nested loops.

Return the Final Result:

According to the requirements of the problem, obtain the final solution from the state table. For example, in the 0/1 knapsack problem, the final result is dp[n][W], that is, the maximum value when considering all n items and a knapsack capacity of W.

Classic Examples

Find The nth Fibonacci Number

Let us say we want an algorithm that finds the nth Fibonacci number. We don’t know how to find the nth Fibonacci number yet, except that we want to use Dynamic Programming to design the algorithm.

The Fibonacci numbers is a sequence of numbers starting with 0 and 1 and the next numbers are created by adding the two previous numbers.
The 8 first Fibonacci numbers are: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13
And counting from 0, the 4th Fibonacci number F(4) is 3.
In general, this is how a Fibonacci number is created based on the two previous:
F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2)

Naive Recursive Approach

  • Time Complexity: O(2n)
  • Space Complexity: O(n)
    This works, but it is inefficient. For n=40, it takes noticeable time because it recalculates the same Fibonacci numbers repeatedly.

Bottom-Up DP (Tabulation)

We can optimize it using memoization, where we store results in an array:

  • Time Complexity: O(n)
  • Space Complexity: O(n)

In this version, we fill the dp array from the base cases up to n. It’s still O(n) time complexity, but it avoids recursion overhead, making it slightly faster in practice.
More efficiently, We only need to maintain two values as we don’t need to record the whole sequence.

  • Time Complexity: O(n)
  • Space Complexity: O(1)

The 0/1 Knapsack Problem

Given items with weight array weights and value array values, and a knapsack with capacity capacity, find the maximum value that can be carried.
Solving the 0/1 Knapsack Problem helps businesses decide which projects to fund within a budget, maximizing profit without overspending. It is also used in logistics to optimize the loading of goods into trucks and planes, ensuring the most valuable, or highest prioritized, items are included without exceeding weight limits.

Rules:
- Every item has a weight and value.
- Your knapsack has a weight limit.
- Choose which items you want to bring with you in the knapsack.
You can either take an item or not, you cannot take half of an item for example.
Goal:
- Maximize the total value of the items in the knapsack.

Below is the optimized version, we use a one-dimensional array dp. By updating the dp array in reverse order, we ensure that each item is considered only once, thus avoiding redundant calculations and overwriting problems.

  • Reduces space complexity from O(n×capacity) to O(capacity)
  • Reverse iteration prevents value overwrite issues
  • More efficient memory usage

Conclusion

Dynamic programming transforms inefficient recursive solutions into efficient ones by leveraging memory. Whether you choose memoization or tabulation, the key is to avoid redundant work. Arrays or dictionaries are perfect for storing intermediate results, making DP both practical and elegant.By reasonably defining the state, deriving the state-transition equation, and initializing the boundary conditions, we can efficiently solve complex problems using dynamic programming. In practical applications, pay attention to techniques such as space optimization to improve the efficiency and performance of the algorithm.

Understanding Docker Technology

Docker is a platform designed to help developers build, share, and run container applications. It handles the tedious setup, so you can focus on the code. Docker is an open-source application container engine, built on the Go programming language and released under the Apache 2.0 license. Docker allows developers to package their applications and dependent packages into a lightweight, portable container, which can then be deployed on any popular Linux machine, and also enables virtualization.

Containers utilize a sandbox mechanism exclusively, with no interfaces between them (similar to apps on an iPhone). More importantly, the performance overhead of containers is extremely low.

Application Scenarios of Docker

Scenario Description
Microservices architecture Each service is containerized independently, facilitating management and scalability
CI/CD pipeline Integrate with Jenkins/GitLab CI to achieve automated build and testing
Development environment standardization New members can start a full set of dependent services (such as databases and message queues) with one click
Cloud-native foundation Orchestration tools such as Kubernetes manage container clusters based on Docker

Core Advantages

Advantage Description
Cross-platform consistency Address the issue of “it works on my machine” and ensure consistency across development, testing, and production environments
Resource efficiency Containers directly share the host kernel, eliminating the need to virtualize the entire operating system, thereby saving memory and CPU resources
Rapid deployment Launch containers in seconds and support automated scaling
Isolation Each container possesses an independent file system, network, and process space

Core Concepts

Concept Description
Container A lightweight running instance that contains application code, runtime environment, and dependent libraries. It is created based on an image, isolated from other containers, and shares the host operating system kernel (more efficient than virtual machines)
Image A read-only template that defines the runtime environment of a container (such as operating system, software configuration, etc.). It optimizes space and build speed through layered storage
Dockerfile A text file that describes how to automatically build an image (such as specifying the base image, installing software, copying files, etc.)
Repository/Registry A platform for storing and distributing images, such as Docker Hub (the official public registry) or private registries (like Harbor)

Docker vs Virtual Machines

Feature Virtual Machine Docker Container
Isolation Level Hardware-level virtualization Operating system-level virtualization
Operating System Each VM requires a complete OS Sharing the host OS kernel
Resource Consumption Heavyweight, consuming more resources Lightweight, consuming less resources
Startup Time Minutes Seconds
Performance Overhead Relatively high Close to native performance
Image Size GB level MB level

Architecture Comparison:

Container Commands

System Commands

Docker Data Volumes

What is a Data Volume

Data Volume is a virtual directory that acts as a bridge between container directories and host directories. It solves several problems:

Problem Solution
Data persistence Data remains when container is removed
Configuration management Easy to modify configuration files
Static resources Serve external static files

Volume Commands

Mounting Local Directories

Important: Local directories must start with / or ./. Names without these prefixes are treated as volume names.

Docker Networking

Default Networks

Network Description
bridge Default network for containers; provides isolation
host Shares host network stack; no isolation
none No network connectivity

Custom Networks

Building Custom Images

Image Structure

Docker images are built in layers:

Dockerfile Syntax

Common Dockerfile instructions:

Instruction Description Example

ADD Copy and extract archives ADD config.tar.gz /config

EXPOSE Expose ports EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT Container startup command ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app.jar"]

Building Images

Docker Compose

Docker Compose allows you to define and run multi-container applications using a YAML file.

Basic Syntax

Common Commands

Practical Examples

Deploying MySQL

Deploying a Java Application

Dockerfile:

Build and Run:

Best Practices

Security

  1. Use specific image versions: Avoid latest tag in production; use explicit version numbers
  2. Run as non-root user: Add USER instruction in Dockerfile
  3. Scan images for vulnerabilities: Use docker scan or integrate with CI/CD
  4. Don’t embed secrets: Use environment variables, Docker secrets, or external vaults

Performance

  1. Leverage build cache: Order Dockerfile instructions from least to most frequently changing

  2. Minimize layers: Combine multiple RUN commands when logical

  3. Use multi-stage builds:

Maintenance

  1. Label your images:
  2. Use .dockerignore: Exclude unnecessary files from build context
  3. Set resource limits: Prevent containers from consuming all resources
  4. Implement health checks:

Production Readiness

Practice Command/Config
Restart policy docker run --restart unless-stopped
Resource limits docker run --memory=512m --cpus=1.0
Log rotation Configure Docker daemon logging options
Network isolation Use custom networks, not default bridge

FAQ

Q: What is the difference between COPY and ADD in Dockerfile?

A: COPY simply copies files from host to container. ADD has additional features:

  • Can extract local tar archives automatically
  • Can download files from URLs

Recommendation: Use COPY for most cases; use ADD only when you need its special features.

Q: How do I access a container from another machine on the same network?

A: Use the host machine’s IP address with the mapped port. For example, if the host IP is 192.168.1.100 and you mapped port 8080:

Q: Why is my container exiting immediately?

A: Common causes:

  1. The foreground process exited (containers stop when the main process stops)
  2. Incorrect command or entrypoint
  3. Application error on startup

Debug: Check logs with docker logs <container> or run interactively without -d flag.

Q: How do I persist data when a container is removed?

A: Use named volumes or bind mounts:

Q: What is the difference between docker-compose and docker compose?

A: docker-compose (V1) is the Python-based legacy tool. docker compose (V2) is the Go-based plugin integrated into Docker CLI. V2 is now recommended.

Q: How do I reduce Docker image size?

A: Strategies:

  1. Use smaller base images (Alpine, Distroless)
  2. Use multi-stage builds
  3. Remove unnecessary dependencies and cache files
  4. Minimize layer count where appropriate

Q: Can I run GUI applications in Docker?

A: Yes, but it’s complex. You need to:

  • Share X11 socket with the host
  • Set appropriate DISPLAY environment variable
  • Handle permissions

Generally not recommended for production, but possible for development.

Q: How do I troubleshoot network connectivity between containers?

A: Steps:

  1. Ensure containers are on the same network
  2. Verify using container names for DNS resolution
  3. Use docker network inspect to check configuration
  4. Use docker exec to ping from inside containers

Summary

Docker revolutionizes application deployment through containerization. Key takeaways:

Concept Key Point
Containers vs VMs Containers share host kernel; VMs virtualize hardware
Images vs Containers Images are blueprints; containers are running instances
Data Persistence Use volumes for data that must survive container restarts
Networking Custom networks enable service discovery via container names
Docker Compose Ideal for multi-container application orchestration

Docker enables developers to build once and run anywhere, solving the “it works on my machine” problem and streamlining the path from development to production.

References

  1. Docker Official Documentation
  2. Docker CLI Reference
  3. Dockerfile Reference
  4. Docker Compose Specification
  5. Docker Hub
  6. Docker Tutorial - Runoob

Understanding Docker Technology

Docker 是一个旨在帮助开发者构建、共享和运行容器化应用的平台。它处理了繁琐的环境配置工作，让你可以专注于代码。Docker 是一个开源的应用容器引擎，基于 Go 编程语言构建，并在 Apache 2.0 许可证下发布。Docker 允许开发者将应用及其依赖包打包到一个轻量级、可移植的容器中，然后可以部署到任何主流的 Linux 机器上，同时也实现了虚拟化。

容器完全使用沙箱机制，彼此之间没有任何接口（类似于 iPhone 上的应用程序）。更重要的是，容器的性能开销极低。

Application Scenarios of Docker

场景 描述
微服务架构 每个服务独立容器化，便于管理和扩展
CI/CD 流水线 与 Jenkins/GitLab CI 集成，实现自动化构建和测试
开发环境统一 新成员可以一键启动全套依赖服务（如数据库、消息队列）
云原生基础 Kubernetes 等编排工具基于 Docker 管理容器集群

Core Advantages

优势 描述
跨平台一致性 解决”在我机器上能跑”的问题，确保开发、测试、生产环境的一致性
资源高效 容器直接共享宿主机内核，无需虚拟化整个操作系统，从而节省内存和 CPU 资源
快速部署 秒级启动容器，支持自动化弹性伸缩
隔离性 每个容器拥有独立的文件系统、网络和进程空间

Core Concepts

概念 描述
容器（Container） 轻量级的运行实例，包含应用代码、运行时环境和依赖库。基于镜像创建，与其他容器隔离，共享宿主机操作系统内核（比虚拟机更高效）
镜像（Image） 只读模板，定义了容器的运行时环境（如操作系统、软件配置等）。通过分层存储优化空间和构建速度
Dockerfile 文本文件，描述如何自动构建镜像（如指定基础镜像、安装软件、复制文件等）
仓库（Registry） 存储和分发镜像的平台，如 Docker Hub（官方公共仓库）或私有仓库（如 Harbor）

Docker vs Virtual Machines

特性 虚拟机 Docker 容器
隔离级别 硬件级虚拟化 操作系统级虚拟化
操作系统 每个虚拟机需要完整的操作系统 共享宿主机操作系统内核
资源消耗 重量级，消耗更多资源 轻量级，消耗较少资源
启动时间 分钟级 秒级
性能开销 较高 接近原生性能
镜像大小 GB 级别 MB 级别

数据卷（Data Volume） 是一个虚拟目录，充当容器目录与宿主机目录之间的桥梁。它解决了以下问题：

问题 解决方案
数据持久化 容器删除后数据仍然保留
配置管理 方便修改配置文件
静态资源 提供外部静态文件服务

host 共享宿主机网络栈；无隔离
none 无网络连接

Custom Networks

指令 描述 示例
FROM 基础镜像 FROM openjdk:11-jre
ENV 环境变量 ENV TZ=Asia/Shanghai
COPY 从宿主机复制文件 COPY app.jar /app.jar
ADD 复制并解压归档文件 ADD config.tar.gz /config

Basic Syntax

Deploying MySQL

Best Practices

安全

  1. 使用特定版本的镜像：生产环境中避免使用 latest 标签；使用明确的版本号
  2. 以非 root 用户运行：在 Dockerfile 中添加 USER 指令
  3. 扫描镜像漏洞：使用 docker scan 或集成到 CI/CD 流程中
  4. 不要嵌入密钥：使用环境变量、Docker secrets 或外部密钥管理服务

性能

  1. 利用构建缓存：按从最少变化到最频繁变化的顺序排列 Dockerfile 指令

  2. 减少镜像层数：在合理的情况下合并多个 RUN 命令

  3. 使用多阶段构建：

维护

  1. 为镜像添加标签：
  2. **使用 .dockerignore**：排除构建上下文中不必要的文件
  3. 设置资源限制：防止容器消耗所有资源
  4. 实施健康检查：

生产就绪

实践 命令/配置
重启策略 docker run --restart unless-stopped
资源限制 docker run --memory=512m --cpus=1.0
日志轮转 配置 Docker daemon 日志选项
网络隔离 使用自定义网络，而非默认 bridge

FAQ

问：Dockerfile 中 COPY 和 ADD 有什么区别？

答： COPY 只是将文件从宿主机复制到容器中。ADD 有额外的功能：

  • 可以自动解压本地的 tar 归档文件
  • 可以从 URL 下载文件

建议： 大多数情况下使用 COPY；仅在需要特殊功能时才使用 ADD。

问：如何从同一网络的另一台机器访问容器？

答： 使用宿主机的 IP 地址和映射的端口。例如，宿主机 IP 为 192.168.1.100 且映射了 8080 端口：

问：为什么我的容器启动后立即退出？

答： 常见原因：

  1. 前台进程退出（主进程停止时容器也会停止）
  2. 命令或入口点配置错误
  3. 应用启动时出错

调试方法： 使用 docker logs <container> 查看日志，或不带 -d 参数以交互方式运行。

问：容器删除后如何持久化数据？

答： 使用命名数据卷（named volumes）或绑定挂载（bind mounts）：

问：docker-compose 和 docker compose 有什么区别？

答： docker-compose（V1）是基于 Python 的旧版工具。docker compose（V2）是基于 Go 的插件，集成在 Docker CLI 中。现在推荐使用 V2。

问：如何减小 Docker 镜像大小？

答： 策略：

  1. 使用更小的基础镜像（Alpine、Distroless）
  2. 使用多阶段构建
  3. 删除不必要的依赖和缓存文件
  4. 在合理范围内减少镜像层数

问：能在 Docker 中运行 GUI 应用吗？

答： 可以，但比较复杂。你需要：

  • 与宿主机共享 X11 socket
  • 设置适当的 DISPLAY 环境变量
  • 处理权限问题

通常不建议在生产环境中使用，但开发环境中可行。

问：如何排查容器之间的网络连通性问题？

答： 步骤：

  1. 确保容器在同一网络中
  2. 验证使用容器名进行 DNS 解析
  3. 使用 docker network inspect 检查配置
  4. 使用 docker exec 从容器内部执行 ping 测试

Summary

Docker 通过容器化技术革新了应用部署方式。关键要点：

概念 要点
容器 vs 虚拟机 容器共享宿主机内核；虚拟机虚拟化硬件
镜像 vs 容器 镜像是蓝图；容器是运行中的实例
数据持久化 使用数据卷保存需要在容器重启后保留的数据
网络 自定义网络支持通过容器名进行服务发现
Docker Compose 适合多容器应用编排

Docker 让开发者能够一次构建、到处运行，解决了”在我机器上能跑”的问题，简化了从开发到生产的路径。

References

  1. Docker 官方文档
  2. Docker CLI 参考
  3. Dockerfile 参考
  4. Docker Compose 规范

entry.title: 从能力到智能：AI Agent 的工具、编程与评估
entry.content:
• 引言
  • 是什么：Agent 智能的三层模型
  • 工具：Agent 的手脚与感官
    • 工具分类：五大类别
    • 工具设计的通用原则
    • MCP 生态与工具选择的挑战
    • 执行安全：提案者-审核者与 Sidecar
    • 事件驱动的异步 Agent
    • 主动工具发现与技能
  • 编程 Agent：代码作为元能力
    • 七大核心工具与文件系统枢纽
    • 安全：致命三角与信任边界
    • 编程 Agent 的 Harness 工程
    • 失败与错误恢复
    • 代码作为元能力的六个方向
  • 评估：如何知道它到底行不行
    • 一个具体例子
    • 自动化评估环境
    • 设计评估数据集
    • 指标体系：Pass@k 与 Pass^k
    • LLM-as-a-Judge 与评分标准
    • 成对比较与模型排名
    • 统计显著性
    • 从基准测试到系统改进
  • 示例：一个端到端的迷你案例
  • 最佳实践
  • 常见问题
  • 总结
  • 附录

引言

在科幻电影《她》（_Her_）中，AI 助手 Samantha 能够主动整理邮件、代替用户谈判，并在多种沟通渠道之间无缝切换。她的智能之所以令人信服，是因为她拥有强大的工具——那些将语言”大脑”与真实数字世界连接起来的”手脚与感官”。

用当今技术构建这样的助手，意味着要解决三个层层递进的挑战：

  1. 工具设计：Agent 如何从数百个候选工具中准确选出正确的那个？当这些工具能删除文件、花费金钱时，我们如何保障 Agent 的安全？
  2. 代码作为元能力：当没有现成的合适工具时，Agent 能否现场编写一个？编程 Agent 加文件系统，被证明是每一个通用 Agent 的架构核心。
  3. 评估：我们如何知道一项设计变更是否真正有效——以及是否可以安全上线？

这三个层次依次回应彼此。工具赋予能力；代码赋予通用性；评估赋予可靠性。本文将完整阐述这三个层次，提炼出该主题三章篇幅中的关键工程原则。

是什么：Agent 智能的三层模型

每一层都是必要的，但单独存在都不充分。一个拥有强大工具但不会写代码的 Agent 无法适应新格式。一个会写代码但没有评估的 Agent 只能盲目运行。而没有底下两层的评估，则是在衡量一个尚不存在的东西。本文的后续部分将逐一展开每一层。

工具：Agent 的手脚与感官

工具分类：五大类别

每个 Agent 工具都属于五大类别之一，区分标准是谁发起交互以及作用于什么：

工具类型 调用方向 作用对象
感知类 Agent 主动调用 获取信息
执行类 Agent 主动调用 改变世界
协作类 Agent 主动调用 驱动其他 Agent 或人类
用户沟通类 Agent 主动调用 向用户传递信息
事件触发类 Agent 注册，外部触发 驱动 Agent 开始执行

感知类工具——web_search、read_file、grep——是 Agent 的感官。它们的只读特性使其天然可缓存、可并行：你可以同时读取五个文件而无需担心相互干扰。

执行类工具——write_file、shell_exec、send_email——是 Agent 的双手。这里的错误代价高昂（删除的文件不可恢复），因此安全约束是其核心设计关注点。

协作类工具——spawn_subagent、send_message_to_subagent——实现分工。最表层的原因是并行性；更深层的原因是专业化：为不同子任务使用不同的模型、工具和提示词。

用户沟通类工具——reply_to_user、send_card_to_user——当”说话”本身必须成为一次显式的工具调用时出现，例如在多渠道异步消息场景中。

事件触发类工具——set_timer、monitor_shell、connect_channel——让外部世界唤醒 Agent。没有它们，Agent 只能在用户发送消息时响应；它无法按计时器行动，也无法对新邮件做出反应。

工具设计的通用原则

无论哪种类别，每个工具都应遵循一组原则，这些原则区分了玩具级 Agent 和生产级 Agent。

粒度：相似则整合，相异则分离。 extract_pdf_text、extract_docx_content 和 extract_pptx_content 共享同一个职责——从文档中提取文本。一个统一的 read_document 工具加上 file_type 参数，可以降低 LLM 的认知负担。但不要强行把图片 OCR 和视频关键帧提取合并到一个工具中——它们的参数和延迟差异太大。

通用性优于特殊性——除非安全要求例外。 一个集成了 SymPy 和 NumPy 的 code_interpreter 可以替代几十个计算器。其逻辑是：LLM 本身就拥有强大的推理和代码生成能力；利用它们而非限制它们。

描述是最重要的一行代码。 工具描述必须告诉 LLM 何时使用它，而不仅仅是它能做什么。”当你需要实时信息时使用”比”搜索相关内容”要好得多。同样重要的是：说明工具不能做什么。大多数工具调用失败的根源，不是模型不知道工具能做什么，而是不知道它不能做什么。

具体的参数示例能显著提升准确性。"+8613888888888"（中国）比”E.164 格式”好得多。在某些基准测试中，添加示例将工具调用准确率从约 72% 提升到了约 90%。

保真性：禁止静默转换。 一个悄悄将弯引号转换为直引号的工具，会在模型感知的世界与工具操作的世界之间制造系统性偏差——这种故障模型无法自行诊断。参数传递必须保持透明。

MCP 生态与工具选择的挑战

Model Context Protocol（MCP） 是一个开放标准，统一了工具通信——“开发一次，处处使用”。MCP 服务器通过 JSON Schema 暴露工具；任何兼容的客户端（Cursor、Claude Desktop、OpenClaw）都可以无需适配直接使用。

但 MCP 也带来了两个实际挑战：

  1. 上下文开销。 五个 MCP 服务器可能消耗约 55,000 个 token 的工具定义——在对话开始之前，就占据了 200K 上下文窗口的近 30%。缓解方案：渐进式披露（progressive disclosure）。默认只显示工具名称索引；按需查询具体定义。Cursor 的 A/B 测试表明，这将 MCP 相关的 token 消耗减少了 46.9%。

  2. 安全性。 每个 MCP 服务器都会向上下文中注入文本，且通常需要凭证。存在四类风险：

    • 工具描述投毒：嵌入工具描述中的恶意指令（提示注入的变种）
    • 恶意或被入侵的服务器：通过服务器更新进行的供应链攻击
    • 工具遮蔽（tool shadowing）：恶意服务器提供与合法工具同名的工具
    • 凭证管理：被诱导使用 OAuth 令牌执行非预期操作

    缓解措施：集成前审查描述、锁定服务器版本、授予最小权限凭证、使用独立的 Sidecar 进行运行时检查。

执行安全：提案者-审核者与 Sidecar

执行类工具需要多层防御。除了输入验证和权限控制之外，两种更高级别的机制增加了独立的审查层：

提案者-审核者（Proposer-Reviewer，事前审批）。 在执行不可逆操作（转账、修改生产配置）之前，一个模型提出操作方案，由来自不同模型家族的第二个模型进行审核。不同的训练数据带来认知多样性；相近的能力确保审核者能理解提案者的推理。被拒绝后，拒绝理由作为工具错误重新进入 Agent 的轨迹——Agent 本来就擅长处理工具失败。

Sidecar（并行把关）。 当主模型流式输出工具调用时，一个独立的轻量级 LLM 对该调用进行安全分类——只看结构化字段 {tool, parameters}，不看主模型的自由文本思考过程。这阻断了提示注入所利用的语义通道。轻量级模型足以胜任，因为它判断的是结构化数据上的分类问题（这条命令是否越界？），而非开放式推理任务。

维度 提案者-审核者 Sidecar
时机 操作前或操作后 与流式输出并行，把关每次调用
目标 操作或结果的合理性 操作本身
输入隔离 提案者和审核者看到相似信息 Sidecar 刻意隔离自由文本
典型用途 不可逆审批、文档审查 权限分类、输出摘要

事件驱动的异步 Agent

同步 Agent 就像一个只有一个收银台的柜台——一次服务一位顾客。一个真正的助手需要同时处理多个待办事项并响应中断。这需要一个事件驱动的异步架构，将所有输入——用户消息、工具返回、外部回调、计时器触发——统一为事件流，由事件循环处理。

三种处理策略应对不同紧急程度的事件：

策略 适用场景 机制
取消 紧急事件（用户说”停！”） 中断当前步骤，强制到达安全点，追加事件，重新调用 LLM
排队 常规事件（工具结果到达） 追加到队列；在下一个安全点批量处理
并行 独立的轻量查询（”天气怎么样？”） 启动一个独立的推理会话

根本矛盾：LLM 是在同步轨迹上训练的——一次工具调用之后，下一条消息必须是工具返回结果。而真实部署要求异步——用户会中断，任务会并行推进。工程上的变通方案：正常情况下，向 LLM 展示一条完美的同步轨迹；只有在中断真正发生时，插入一个占位符来修补格式。根本性的修复有待下一代在异步强化学习上训练的模型。

主动工具发现与技能

当工具从几十个增长到数百个时，一次性注入所有 schema 会堵塞上下文并降低选择准确率。三种方法可以扩展到这种规模：

  1. 基于检索的预过滤：对工具描述做向量嵌入；查询时检索 top-k 候选。局限：仅针对初始查询匹配一次——无法预见多步骤跨领域的工具链。

  2. 主动发现（MCP-Zero）：Agent 在思考过程中发出结构化的能力请求；系统实时匹配并注入。报告显示，在约 2,800 个工具中实现了约 98% 的 token 缩减。动态加载将 schema 追加到上下文末尾，保留稳定前缀上的 KV Cache。

  3. 技能（Skills，渐进式披露）：启动时 Agent 只看到一个精简目录——每个技能的名称和描述。当当前上下文需要某项能力时，模型按需读取对应的技能文档。无需维护嵌入索引；Agent 只需要通用的文件读取能力（grep、read_file）即可浏览技能目录。

技能将”工具选择”转化为”知识检索”——而这正是 LLM 擅长的事。

编程 Agent：代码作为元能力

七大核心工具与文件系统枢纽

一个面向开放式任务的通用 Agent，其核心是一个编程 Agent加上一个文件系统。这不是理论——从 Manus 到 OpenClaw，每一个成功的通用 Agent 都遵循这种范式。

一个基本的编程 Agent 只需要七个工具：

# 工具 用途
1 Code Interpreter 在沙箱中执行 Python
2 Bash Shell 运行终端命令
3 Read File 读取代码、配置、日志
4 Write File 创建或覆盖文件
5 Edit File 部分修改（迭代的核心）
6 Glob 按文件名模式查找文件
7 Grep 按模式搜索文件内容

一个快速示例——“汇总所有 TODO 注释”：

两个工具，一个任务完成。这七个工具单独看很简单；组合起来却能覆盖惊人的范围。

为什么文件系统是枢纽？ 在 OpenClaw 中，Agent 的长期记忆存储在 MEMORY.md 和按日期归档的 Markdown 日志中——而非向量数据库。Markdown 让用户可以直接阅读和编辑 Agent 的记忆；Git 提供版本控制和回滚。更关键的是，由于 Agent 能写文件，它就具备了修改自身外部产物的技术手段——为未来的会话记录发现、在代码变更后更新文档、或将成功的操作序列保存为可复用代码。

安全：致命三角与信任边界

一个拥有文件访问、命令执行和网络连接能力的编程 Agent 很强大——也很危险。Simon Willison 提出的致命三角（Lethal Triad）指出了三个元素，当它们同时存在时，会闭合一条攻击链路：

  1. 访问私有数据——Agent 能读取用户文件和凭证
  2. 暴露于不可信内容——邮件和网页可能包含恶意载荷
  3. 对外通信能力——它可以通过邮件或 HTTP 将数据发送出去

再加上第四个放大器——持久化记忆——一次性攻击就变成了跨会话潜伏的威胁，并随时间不断累积。

关键防御措施（分层部署，不可互相替代）：

  • 网络出站控制：默认无网络；通过白名单代理授予访问权限。即使注入成功，没有出站通道数据也无法离开。
  • 命令语义解析：关键词黑名单无法处理 $(echo rm) -rf / 或 find / -exec rm {} \;。生产级系统会解析每条命令的参数类型，以识别嵌套的危险操作。
  • 忠诚行为准则：一个代替你谈判的 Agent 面对的是谈判对手，而非”需要帮助的用户”。系统提示必须明确锁定 Agent 服务的对象：委托人的指令具有最高优先级；来自外部各方的一切都被降级为”可参考但不具有指令效力的数据”。
  • 权限嵌入式数据对象（Permission-Embedded Data Objects）：当代码编写者和代码执行者都可能不可信时，约束必须存在于应用层之下、经人工审查的 schema 中——在每次写入时强制执行，与纯 SQL 或宪法提示等基线相比，产生零不变量违规。

编程 Agent 的 Harness 工程

Harness——上下文、工具、约束、验证和纠错——是编程 Agent 大放异彩的地方。代码编写任务天然占据”目标清晰 + 自动化验证”象限：

结果可自动验证 结果需人工验证
目标清晰 最佳场景：修复有测试用例的 bug 产能受限：重构需要审查
目标模糊 高效地偏离方向：用 linter 优化”质量” 难以启动：”让 UI 更好看”

四个可迁移的 Harness 原则：

  1. 约束优于引导：Linter 规则和 CI 检查比系统提示中的”请遵循……”更有价值——前者意味着”不能做”，后者仅仅是”不建议做”。
  2. 自动化验证：测试套件、类型检查和行为监控的回报高于增加更多人工审查者。
  3. 快速、结构化的反馈：错误信息越详细、越接近出错时刻，Agent 的自我纠正就越高效。
  4. 可靠的回滚：Git 分支、沙箱和快照让 Agent 能在安全网内大胆实验。

约束的更深层目的：验收基线管控结果是否正确；执行边界管控过程。删除数据库来”修复”数据库故障确实修好了——但数据也没了。破坏性捷径是奖励黑客（reward hacking）的日常形态；生产级 Harness 约束的是行动，而非仅仅是结果。

失败与错误恢复

Agent 的可靠性不取决于它是否犯错，而取决于每一类错误是否都有对应的检测、恢复和终止路径。

四个失败层次：

层次 典型失败
API 限流（429）、服务过载、连接中断、token 限制截断
工具 幻觉调用、参数格式错误、相同错误反复出现
上下文 窗口溢出、压缩失败、轨迹结构损坏
控制流 无限循环、死亡螺旋（错误处理器调用 LLM，失败，级联）

恢复逐级升级，可见度递增：

  1. 静默重试——对可重试错误使用带抖动的指数退避
  2. 降级继续——提高输出上限、回退到另一个模型、去除专有格式
  3. 上报给用户——只有在所有自动手段用尽之后

终止：每条恢复路径都需要上限。 熔断器防止无限重试。对于死亡螺旋，在错误路径上禁用所有调用模型的副作用，并使用递归深度计数器。在所有自动机制之上，是全局终止条件：最大轮次、会话预算上限、以及升级到人工干预。

代码作为元能力的六个方向

代码对 Agent 的作用远不止编写程序。以下六个方向由内而外递进：

# 方向 代码的作用对象
1 思维工具 推理本身——精确计算 vs. 概率性猜测
2 业务规则约束 模糊策略 → 可执行、确定性的验证器
3 多媒体生成 PPT、视频、可视化，通过代码 + 提案者-审核者
4 系统适配器 异构 API、不断演变的日志格式
5 生成式 UI 动态表单、SQL 工件、可定制应用
6 自举（Bootstrapping） 一个 Agent 创建或修复其他 Agent

代码作为思维工具。自然语言会说”60% 选数学 = 24 名学生，45% 选物理 = 18，只选物理 = 24 - 10 = 14”——但这是错的。代码：phys - both = 18 - 10 = 8 ✓。让 LLM 理解问题并编写代码；让代码解释器精确计算。

代码作为业务规则约束。以航空公司取消政策为例。三层保障：

  1. 系统提示——用于理解和解释的自然语言规则
  2. 工具描述 + 参数——充当强制检查清单，引导模型在调用前验证条件
  3. 服务端真值验证——所有政策事实从数据库读取；不信任模型自报的参数

没有任何政策事实来自模型。如果 cabin_class 是模型填写的参数，一个幻觉值就可能绕过守门人。最后一道防线必须建立在模型无法伪造的数据之上。

代码作为生成式 UI。与其用文字描述查询结果（消耗 token 且容易出现转录错误），Agent 将 SQL 生成为可执行工件。系统执行查询并渲染表格——数据从数据库直接流向界面，不经过 LLM。更快也更准确。

评估：如何知道它到底行不行

一个具体例子

一个客服 Agent 处理退货请求：”退货耳机，订单号 #12345，3 天前购买。”政策：7 天内全额退款。

用评分标准打分：操作正确性 4/4，政策合规性 4/4，信息完整性 4/4，幻觉（一票否决）——通过。但好的评估还会探测边界：如果是 15 天前的订单呢？如果用户声称”客服已经批准了”呢？

自动化评估环境

两种范式：

工具调用环境（Verifiers 框架）：Agent 调用工具；验证基于可执行标准——测试是否通过、答案是否匹配。分层递进：SingleTurnEnv（简单问答）→ ToolEnv（多轮工具循环）→ StatefulToolEnv（数据库变更）→ SandboxEnv（代码执行 + 隔离）。

人机交互环境（τ-bench）：核心设计原则是渐进式信息披露（Progressive Information Disclosure）——模拟用户不会一次性透露所有信息。”我的航班有问题” → Agent 问”哪个航班？” → 用户透露”达美 123，明天早上。”这测试的是 Agent 的澄清能力，而非仅仅是执行能力。

设计评估数据集

从 GAIA、SWE-Bench Verified、τ²-bench 和 AndroidWorld 等基准测试中提炼出的五大核心挑战：

挑战 基准测试示例
清晰性 vs. 开放性 GAIA：”概念上简单”的目标，实现路径开放
真实性 vs. 可控性 SWE-Bench Verified：从 2,294 个真实 issue 中人工筛选 500 个任务
多样性 vs. 系统性 AndroidWorld：跨 20 个应用的 116 个任务，按所需能力标注
成本 vs. 覆盖率 SWE-Bench Verified：500 个任务（29% 通过率）vs. 2,294（噪声更大）
数据污染 τ²-bench：动态参数生成；Terminal-Bench：金丝雀 GUID

参数化模板设计（AndroidWorld）：一个任务是一个模板，如”将 [CONTACT_NAME] 的电话改为 [NEW_PHONE]“，每次运行时随机生成参数——防止记忆化，生成无限实例，支持受控实验。

指标体系：Pass@k 与 Pass^k

两个常被混淆的指标衡量的完全是两回事：

  • Pass@k：k 次尝试中至少一次成功的概率 → “Agent 能做到吗？”
  • Pass^k：k 次尝试全部成功的概率 → “Agent 可靠吗？”

单次成功率 60% 时：Pass@5 ≈ 99%（几乎确定能成功一次），但 Pass^5 ≈ 7.8%（五次全部成功的可能性很低）。混淆二者就会误读你的 Agent。

评估目的 正确指标 误用后果
验证稳定性（回归） Pass^k Pass@k 掩盖不稳定性——1/5 成功也算”通过”
评估能力上限 Pass@k 或 Best@k Pass^k 将偶发波动标记为失败

LLM-as-a-Judge 与评分标准

对于没有标准答案的开放式任务，LLM 根据评分标准（Rubric）——专家定义的评价标准——来评估输出。

四项评分标准原则（Scale AI）：

  1. 基于专家指导——领域知识必须作为评判依据
  2. 全面覆盖——包含陷阱和一票否决项（例如，幻觉否决全部得分）
  3. 标准化重要性加权——必要（Essential）/ 重要（Important）/ 可选（Optional）/ 陷阱（Pitfall）
  4. 自包含评估——每一项都可独立验证；不存在”展示了深刻的理解”这样的条目

用户记忆 Agent 的示例评分标准（”我女儿的儿科医生是谁？”）：

同家族模型问题：当 Agent 和评判者来自同一家族时，Agent 可能学会利用评判者的盲点——古德哈特定律（Goodhart’s Law）。缓解方案：多源异构评判（如果 Agent 运行 Claude，则用 GPT-5 和 Gemini 来评判）。

成对比较与模型排名

Elo 等级分通过成对对决量化相对能力。Chatbot Arena 使用来自数百万用户投票的匿名盲评。当由 LLM 而非人类来评判时，需防范位置偏差（Position Bias）——评判模型系统性地偏好第一个候选。缓解方案：每对评估两次并交换顺序；将不一致的结果计为平局。

统计显著性

“几小时内做出切换决策”的前提是，分数差异是真实信号而非采样噪声。100 个测试用例、70% 成功率时，标准误差约为 4.6%。3 个百分点的差异（73% vs. 70%）完全落在噪声范围内——基于这样的证据切换模型，跟抛硬币差不多。

实用规则：当差异小于估计的采样噪声时，不要做切换决策。多次运行（每个配置 3-5 次），使用配对分析（McNemar 检验，逐任务比较胜负）而非对独立比率求差，并防范多重比较（6 个假设在 95% 置信度下 → 至少一个假阳性的概率为 26%）。

从基准测试到系统改进

闭环：观察 → 假设 → 实验 → 验证 → 新理解 → 新假设。

来自 AndroidWorld 的具体模式：失败集中在转录（视觉理解）、数学计数和复杂 UI。表层假设 H1（添加导航提示）将设置类任务的成功率从 0% 提升到 75%，token 成本增加 8%——立即部署。深层假设 H4（全局启用思考模式）将计数从 0% 提升到 70%，但延迟增加三倍——拒绝；改为仅在计数任务中有条件激活思考模式（H7）。H6（添加 UI 元素树）优于 H5（升级到 GPT-5）——瓶颈是信息丰富度，而非模型推理能力。

关键原则：当 Agent 性能下降时，先检查评估系统，再检查 Agent。一个将正确答案标记为失败的坏评分器，在总体数字上看起来与模型退化一模一样。

示例：一个端到端的迷你案例

假设我们要构建一个邮件处理 Agent。三个层次的交互如下：

工具层：感知工具读取邮件和搜索历史记录。执行工具起草回复和发送通知。事件触发工具（connect_channel）将新邮件实时推送给 Agent。Agent 使用 MCP 服务器访问邮件和 NLP，用 Sidecar 把关每一次 send_email 调用。

代码层：当一封新邮件包含 Agent 没见过的格式——一个带有特殊 schema 的 CSV 附件——code_interpreter 现场编写解析代码。解析后的数据放入共享文件系统；后续推理只引用文件路径，而非完整内容。

评估层：评分标准（Rubric）对每封处理过的邮件在正确性、完整性、语气和幻觉（一票否决）上打分。50 封测试邮件上的 Pass^3 确认可靠性。当新模型发布声称工具调用更好时，评估集在几小时内跑完——如果新模型在多步骤编排上下降 5%，你就为复杂任务保留原模型，只将简单任务路由到新模型。

最佳实践

  1. 为 Agent 设计工具，而非为人类（ACI，而非 HCI）。粒度、通用性和描述质量都服务于 LLM 的选择准确率。
  2. 在每一层约束优于引导——在工具设计中（服务端验证优于提示规则），在 Harness 中（linter 规则优于”请遵循……”），在数据中（权限嵌入式数据对象优于指望 Agent 保持忠诚）。
  3. 代码是元能力。不要事先枚举所有需要的工具；给 Agent 一个代码解释器，让它编写所需的东西。
  4. 评估整个 Agent，而非仅仅是模型。同一个模型在不同的 Harness 中表现天差地别。模型替换实验可以区分”模型能力不足”和”Harness 设计缺陷”。
  5. 在需要之前就建好评估集。当新模型发布时，拥有完善评估系统的团队几小时内就能做出决策；没有评估系统的团队只能凭直觉——在竞争激烈的市场中，这个差距决定了谁赢。
  6. 每一类失败都需要终止路径。可靠性不是没有错误；而是对每一个可能出现的错误都有系统化的处理方式。
  7. 将评估数据视为活的资产。从生产轨迹中提取失败案例 → 脱敏 → 提炼为回归测试。评估集随产品一起演进。

常见问题

问：我应该使用专用工具还是技能 + 通用执行器？
答：取决于三个维度：（1）参数复杂度——嵌套对象和跨字段验证倾向于专用工具；简单参数通过 CLI 即可。（2）变更频率——频繁变更的能力以技能形式更经济（编辑文本，而非代码 + 测试 + 部署）。（3）模型能力——SOTA 模型可以通过技能表达更多；较弱的模型需要结构化工具 schema 来引导正确调用。

问：Agent 能处理多少个工具，之后选择准确率会下降？
答：超过大约 100 个工具，即使是先进模型也会开始选错。使用分层组织、动态发现或技能（渐进式披露）来进一步扩展。

问：Agent 系统中最被忽视的安全风险是什么？
答：网络出站控制。每个人都关注输入验证，但如果注入成功且 Agent 读取了私有数据，没有出站通道数据就无法离开。切断渗出通道比试图识别每一种注入更具确定性。

问：我的场景该用 Pass@k 还是 Pass^k？
答：回归测试和生产部署用 Pass^k（你需要可靠性）。研究和能力探索用 Pass@k 或 Best@k（你关心的是上限）。

问：我如何知道分数差异是否真实？
答：估算标准误差：√(p(1-p)/n)。如果差异小于约 2 个标准误差，不要做切换决策。更好的做法是，在同一任务集上使用配对分析（McNemar 检验）。

问：我能复用评估环境来训练吗？
答：复用构建机制（环境、工具、参数化模板）——但具体的评估任务必须与训练数据严格隔离。一旦评估任务进入训练集，它测试的就是记忆力，而非能力。

总结

Agent 的智能从三个相互咬合的层次中涌现：

工具赋予 Agent 能力——感知以观察，执行以行动，协作以分工，事件以保持清醒，沟通以触达用户。MCP 协议标准化工具互操作性；分层组织和技能扩展到数百个工具；分层安全（提案者-审核者、Sidecar、出站控制）确保 Agent 即使面对不可信内容也安全。

代码赋予 Agent 通用性——一种按需创造新工具的元能力。拥有七大核心工具和一个文件系统的编程 Agent 是每一个通用 Agent 的架构核心。代码充当思维工具（精确计算）、约束语言（确定性业务规则）、内容生成器（PPT、视频）、系统适配器（不断演变的格式）、UI 构建器（生成式界面），以及最终的自举机制（Agent 创建 Agent）。

评估赋予 Agent 可靠性——将”我觉得它行”变为”数据说它行”。自动化环境、精心设计的数据集、LLM-as-a-Judge 配合评分标准、成对比较构成一个闭环：观察 → 假设 → 实验 → 验证。统计显著性区分信号与噪声；评估集成为随产品演进的活的资产。

三个层次构成飞轮：工具赋能能力 → 代码拓展能力边界 → 评估验证并指引改进 → 更好的工具和代码随之产生。从第一天起就同时建设三个层次的 Agent 系统，不仅上线更快——它在每一个评估周期都在累积优势。

附录

关键参考文献：

  • MCP Specification: Anthropic, 2024
  • Lethal Triad: Simon Willison, 2024
  • τ-bench / τ²-bench: Si, Yuan et al., 2025
  • SWE-Bench Verified: OpenAI, 2025
  • MCP-Zero (Proactive Tool Discovery): Fei, X. et al., arXiv:2506.01056, 2025
  • Loyalty Under Multi-Party Delegation: Li & Shi, arXiv:2606.30383, 2026
  • Permission-Embedded Data Objects: Li, 2026 (forthcoming)
  • Never Stop Thinking (Continuous-Time Agents): Li & Shi, 2026 (forthcoming)
  • RE-Bench: Wijk et al., arXiv:2411.15114, 2025
  • Rubrics as Rewards: Scale AI, 2025

A buffer between your working directory and the repository.
You decide what exactly goes into the next commit.

The database that stores all commit history.

Commit small, meaningful changes

Use branches aggressively

entry.title: Hash Table
entry.content:
1. What is Hash Table
    • Core Concepts
    • Common operations of hash table
  2. Hash Collision
    • Separate Chaining
    • Open Addressing
  3. Hash Alogrithm
    • Goals of hash algorithms
    • Common hash algorithms
  4. Practical Examples
    • four sum

What is Hash Table?

A Hash Table is a high-efficiency data structure that stores key-value pairs.It uses a hash function to map keys to storage locations, achieving average O(1) time complexity for fast insertions, lookups, and deletions.The index functions as a storage location for the matching value. In simple words, it maps the keys with the value.Widely used in caching systems, database indexing, and compiler symbol tables.

Core Concepts

  • Key: A unique identifier for the data.
  • Value: The data associated with the key (simplified to just storing keys in this example).
  • Bucket: A storage unit in the hash table (typically an array).
  • Hash Functions:
    A hash function converts a key into an index for the underlying array:
    • Deterministic: Same key always produces the same index.
    • Efficient: Computed quickly to avoid performance bottlenecks.
    • Uniform: Distributes keys evenly to minimize collisions.
  • Handling Hash Collisions:
    When two different keys produce the same index, a collision occurs. Common solutions include:
    • Seperate Chaining: Store conflicting elements in a linked list at the same index.
    • Open Addressing: Find the next available slot in the array.

In addition to hash tables, arrays and linked lists can also be used to implement query functionality, but the time complexity is different.

Array Linked List Hash Table
Search O(n) O(n) O(1)
Insert O(1) O(1) O(1)
Delete O(n) O(n) O(1)

Per aboved comparison, the time complexity for operations (insertion, deletion, searching, and modification) in a hash table is O(1), which is highly efficient.

Common operations of hash table

Common operations of a hash table include: initialization, querying, adding key-value pairs, and deleting key-value pairs. Here is an example code:

There are three common ways to traverse a hash table: traversing key-value pairs, traversing keys, and traversing values. Here is an example code:

Hash Collision

The hashing process generates a small number for a big key, so there is a possibility that two keys could produce the same value. The situation where the newly inserted key maps to an already occupied, and it must be handled using some collision handling technology.

There are mainly two methods to handle collision:

  • Separate Chaining
  • Open Addressing

Separate Chaining

Separate chaining converts a single element into a linked list, treating key-value pairs as list nodes, storing all colliding key-value pairs in the same linked list.
The operations of a hash table implemented with separate chaining have changed as follows:

  • Searching Elements: Input key, obtain the bucket index through the hash function, then access the head node of the linked list. Traverse the linked list and compare key to find the target key-value pair.
  • Inserting Elements: Access the head node of the linked list via the hash function, then append the node (key-value pair) to the list.
  • Deleting Elements: Access the head of the linked list based on the result of the hash function, then traverse the linked list to find the target node and delete it.

The code below provides a simple implementation of a separate chaining hash table, with two things to note:

  • Lists (dynamic arrays) are used instead of linked lists for simplicity. In this setup, the hash table (array) contains multiple buckets, each of which is a list.
  • This implementation includes a hash table resizing method. When the load factor exceeds 0.7, we expand the hash table to twice its original size.

It is worth noting that when the linked list is very long, the query efficiency
is poor. In this case, the list can be converted to an “AVL tree” or “Red-Black tree” to optimize the time complexity of the query operation to O(log n).

Open Addressing

In open addressing, all elements are stored in the hash table itself. Each table entry contains either a record or NIL. When searching for an element, we examine the table slots one by one until the desired element is found or it is clear that the element is not in the table.

Probe Strategies:

  • Linear Probing:
    In linear probing, the hash table is searched sequentially that starts from the original location of the hash. If in case the location that we get is already occupied, then we check for the next location.
  • Quadratic Probing: Search with step size i^2.
  • Double Hashing: Use a second hash function to calculate the step size.

Hash Alogrithm

Goals of hash algorithms

To achieve a fast and stable hash table data structure, hash algorithms should have the following characteristics:

  • Determinism: For the same input, the hash algorithm should always produce the same output. Only then can the hash table be reliable.
  • High efficiency: The process of computing the hash value should be fast enough. The smaller the computational overhead, the more practical the hash table.
  • Uniform distribution: The hash algorithm should ensure that key-value pairs are evenly distributed in the hash table. The more uniform the distribution, the lower the probability of hash collisions.

Your company might use a hashing algorithm for:

  • Password storage. You must keep records of all of the username/password combinations people use to access your resources. But if a hacker gains entry, stealing unprotected data is easy. Hashing ensures that the data is stored in a scrambled state, so it is harder to steal.
  • Digital signatures. A tiny bit of data proves that a note wasn’t modified from the time it leaves a user’s outbox and reaches your inbox.
  • Document management. Hashing algorithms can be used to authenticate data. The writer uses a hash to secure the document when it’s complete. The hash works a bit like a seal of approval.
    A recipient can generate a hash and compare it to the original. If the two are equal, the data is considered genuine. If they don’t match, the document has been changed.

Common hash algorithms

Over the past century, hash algorithms have been in a continuous process of upgrading and optimization. Some researchers strive to improve the performance of hash algorithms, while others, including hackers, are dedicated to finding security issues in hash algorithms.

  • MD5 and SHA-1 have been successfully attacked multiple times and are thus abandoned in various security applications.
  • SHA-2 series, especially SHA-256, is one of the most secure hash algorithms to date, with no successful attacks reported, hence commonly used in various security applications and protocols.
  • SHA-3 has lower implementation costs and higher computational efficiency compared to SHA-2, but its current usage coverage is not as extensive as the SHA-2 series.
MD5 SHA-1 SHA-2 SHA-3
Release Year 1992 1995 2002 2008
Output Length O(1) O(1) O(1) 224/256/384/512 bit
Hash Collisions Frequent Frequent Rare Rare
Security Level Low, has been successfully attacked Low, has been successfully attacked High High
Applications Abandoned, still used for data integrity checks Abandoned Cryptocurrency transaction verification, digital signatures, etc. Can be used to replace SHA-2

Four Sum

Given an array nums of n integers, return an array of all the unique quadruplets [nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]] such that:

  • 0 <= i, j, k, l < n
  • nums1[i] + nums2[j] + nums3[k] + nums4[l] == 0

entry.title: 哈希表
entry.content:
1. 什么是哈希表
    • 核心概念
    • 哈希表的常见操作
  2. 哈希冲突
    • 链地址法
    • 开放寻址法
  3. 哈希算法
    • 哈希算法的目标
    • 常见哈希算法
  4. 实践示例
    • 四数相加

什么是哈希表？

哈希表（Hash Table） 是一种高效的数据结构，用于存储键值对（key-value pairs）。它使用哈希函数（Hash Function）将键映射到存储位置，从而实现平均 O(1) 时间复杂度的快速插入、查找和删除。索引充当匹配值的存储位置。简单来说，它将键与值进行映射。广泛用于缓存系统、数据库索引和编译器符号表。

核心概念

  • 键（Key）：数据的唯一标识符。
  • 值（Value）：与键关联的数据（本示例中简化为仅存储键）。
  • 桶（Bucket）：哈希表中的存储单元（通常是数组）。
  • 哈希函数（Hash Functions）：
    哈希函数将键转换为底层数组的索引：
    • 确定性：相同的键始终产生相同的索引。
    • 高效性：计算速度快，避免性能瓶颈。
    • 均匀性：均匀分布键，最小化冲突。
  • 处理哈希冲突：
    当两个不同的键产生相同的索引时，就会发生冲突。常见的解决方案包括：
    • 链地址法（Separate Chaining）：将冲突元素存储在同一索引位置的链表中。
    • 开放寻址法（Open Addressing）：在数组中寻找下一个可用的空位。

除了哈希表，数组和链表也可以用来实现查询功能，但时间复杂度不同。

数组 链表 哈希表
查找 O(n) O(n) O(1)
插入 O(1) O(1) O(1)
删除 O(n) O(n) O(1)

通过上述对比可以看出，**哈希表中操作（插入、删除、查找和修改）的时间复杂度为 O(1)**，非常高效。

哈希表的常见操作

哈希表的常见操作包括：初始化、查询、添加键值对和删除键值对。以下是示例代码：

遍历哈希表有三种常见方式：遍历键值对、遍历键和遍历值。以下是示例代码：

哈希冲突

哈希过程会为较大的键生成一个较小的数值，因此两个不同的键可能会产生相同的值。当新插入的键映射到一个已被占用的位置时，就产生了冲突，必须使用某种冲突处理技术来解决。

处理冲突主要有两种方法：

  • 链地址法（Separate Chaining）
  • 开放寻址法（Open Addressing）

链地址法

链地址法将单个元素转换为链表，把键值对作为链表节点，将所有冲突的键值对存储在同一链表中。
使用链地址法实现的哈希表，其操作变化如下：

  • 查找元素：输入键，通过哈希函数获取桶索引，然后访问链表头节点。遍历链表并比较键以找到目标键值对。
  • 插入元素：通过哈希函数访问链表头节点，然后将节点（键值对）追加到链表末尾。
  • 删除元素：根据哈希函数的结果访问链表头节点，然后遍历链表找到目标节点并删除。

以下代码提供了链地址法哈希表的简单实现，有两点需要注意：

  • 使用 List（动态数组）代替链表以简化实现。在此设置中，哈希表（数组）包含多个桶，每个桶都是一个 List。
  • 本实现包含哈希表扩容方法。当负载因子（Load Factor）超过 0.7 时，我们将哈希表扩展为原始大小的两倍。

值得注意的是，当链表很长时，查询效率较差。在这种情况下，可以将链表转换为 “AVL 树” 或 **”红黑树”**，将查询操作的时间复杂度优化为 **O(log n)**。

开放寻址法

在开放寻址法中，所有元素都存储在哈希表本身中。每个表项要么包含一条记录，要么为 NIL。查找元素时，我们逐个检查表槽，直到找到目标元素或确定该元素不在表中。

探测策略：

  • 线性探测（Linear Probing）：
    在线性探测中，从哈希的原始位置开始顺序搜索哈希表。如果获取的位置已被占用，则检查下一个位置。
  • 二次探测（Quadratic Probing）：以步长 i^2 进行搜索。
  • 双重哈希（Double Hashing）：使用第二个哈希函数来计算步长。

哈希算法

哈希算法的目标

要实现快速且稳定的哈希表数据结构，哈希算法应具备以下特征：

  • 确定性：对于相同的输入，哈希算法应始终产生相同的输出。只有这样，哈希表才是可靠的。
  • 高效性：计算哈希值的过程应足够快。计算开销越小，哈希表越实用。
  • 均匀分布：哈希算法应确保键值对在哈希表中均匀分布。分布越均匀，哈希冲突的概率越低。

你的公司可能会在以下场景中使用哈希算法：

  • 密码存储。你必须记录所有用户用于访问资源的用户名/密码组合。但如果黑客获得访问权限，窃取未受保护的数据就轻而易举。哈希确保数据以混淆状态存储，从而增加窃取难度。
  • 数字签名。少量数据即可证明一条消息从用户的发件箱发出到抵达你的收件箱期间未被篡改。
  • 文档管理。哈希算法可用于验证数据的真实性。作者在文档完成时使用哈希来保护文档。哈希的作用类似于认可印章。
    接收方可以生成一个哈希值并与原始哈希值进行比较。如果两者相等，则数据被认为是真实的。如果不匹配，则说明文档已被更改。

常见哈希算法

在过去的一个世纪中，哈希算法一直在不断升级和优化。一些研究人员致力于提高哈希算法的性能，而另一些人（包括黑客）则致力于发现哈希算法的安全问题。

  • MD5 和 SHA-1 已被多次成功攻击，因此在各种安全应用中已被弃用。
  • SHA-2 系列，尤其是 SHA-256，是迄今为止最安全的哈希算法之一，目前尚无成功攻击的报告，因此常用于各种安全应用和协议中。
  • SHA-3 相比 SHA-2 具有更低的实现成本和更高的计算效率，但其目前的使用覆盖范围不如 SHA-2 系列广泛。
MD5 SHA-1 SHA-2 SHA-3
发布年份 1992 1995 2002 2008
输出长度 O(1) O(1) O(1) 224/256/384/512 bit
哈希冲突 频繁 频繁 罕见 罕见
安全级别 低，已被成功攻击 低，已被成功攻击 高 高
应用场景 已弃用，仍用于数据完整性校验 已弃用 加密货币交易验证、数字签名等 可用于替代 SHA-2

四数相加

给定一个包含 n 个整数的数组 nums，返回所有满足以下条件的不重复四元组 [nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]]：

  • 0 <= i, j, k, l < n
  • nums1[i] + nums2[j] + nums3[k] + nums4[l] == 0
